study_identification_part.si_4_title: Structural brain abnormalities and aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia: Mega-analysis of data from 2095 patients and 2861 healthy controls via the ENIGMA consortium

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: This study pooled data from 20 sites participating in the ENIGMA Schizophrenia Working Group. Sites include: COBRE, ESO, FIDMAG, FOR2107, GAP, IGP, IMH, JBNU, MCIC, Montreal, MPRC, NU, Olin, RomeSL, RSCZ, SNUH, UCISZ, UMCU, UNINA, and Zürich. Most sites do not have established dataset names in the provided list - they are site-specific cohorts. COBRE and MCIC are recognized dataset names. The study is best characterized as MULTI-SITE (N>=2) since it aggregates data from 20 different sites across 13 countries.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Data came from the Schizophrenia Working Group of the Enhancing Neuroimaging Genetics through Meta-Analysis (ENIGMA) consortium. Twenty member sites contributed data to the current study. These sites were located in 13 different countries, with their samples totalling 2095 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia ('patients') and 2861 unaffected general population controls ('healthy controls')."

answer.ENIGMA (20 sites): pooled mega-analysis; healthy controls for normative model training; patients for clinical application (deviation calculation and association analysis with aggressive behaviour)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Healthy controls (n=2861 for T1-weighted MRI, n=1461 for DTI) were used to derive normative models using warped Bayesian linear regression. Patients with schizophrenia (n=2095 for T1-weighted MRI, n=734 for DTI) were then run through these normative models to calculate individual-level deviation scores (z-scores) from healthy controls, which were subsequently used to examine associations with aggressive behaviour.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "For every IDP, we derived a normative model in the healthy controls using warped Bayesian linear regression with site, sex, age and -for local IDPs only -a global IDP as predictors... The normative models were then run in the patients to calculate how much they deviated (in z-scores) from healthy controls on an individual level."

model-1.model-name: T1-weighted MRI normative model (grey matter volume)

model-2.model-name: Diffusion-weighted MRI normative model (white matter microstructural integrity)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The study used healthy controls from 20 sites for T1-weighted MRI (total n=2718 based on Table 1 'All' row; abstract states 2861 which may include additional participants) and 9 sites for diffusion-weighted MRI (total n=1461 based on Table 2 'All' row). The train/validation/test split is not explicitly reported; the entire healthy control sample appears to have been used to derive the normative models.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "All 20 sites acquired high-resolution (voxel size of ≤1 mm3) T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging scans... Nine sites also acquired diffusion-weighted images." Table 1: "All... HC n=2718"; Table 2: "All... HC n=1461"; Abstract: "2861 healthy controls"

The 'All' row provides aggregate mean and SD. No separate train-phase statistics are provided as the study does not describe a train/test split for the normative model construction.
